newsitem.title: FRANCE: France asks Britain extend Eurotunnel concession.
newsitem.headline: France asks Britain extend Eurotunnel concession.

text.p: France on Wednesday asked Britain's new Labour government to extend the operating concession for Eurotunnel SA to help the troubled Channel Tunnel rail link, a French foreign ministry spokesman said.

"The financial future of Eurotunnel depends on an extension of the concession," he said after talks in Paris between British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
"The financial future of Eurotunnel interests hundreds of thousands of small shareholders," he said, adding that any extension would not mean any cost to public finances in either nation.

De Charette did not spell out in his talks with Cook how long an extension France wanted. The current concession expires in 2052 and Eurotunnel last month said it had asked the British and French governments to extend it for 999 years.

The French spokesman said Cook, making his first trip abroad since Labour won a crushing election victory over the Conservatives last week, agreed to report back to his cabinet colleagues on de Charette's request.

Eurotunnel's French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle said last month that the company was likely to seek insolvency protection if it fails to win shareholder approval for a restructuring of its mountain of debts.
And he said shareholders would reject the restructuring package if Eurotunnel failed to get an extension to its operating licence.
